prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1290; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a rear-end collision at a slow-moving intersection, with the claimant's vehicle stopped in front. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the file has been opened for bodily injury and property damage.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and show that the damage is mostly in line with the described impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos and the account given are the main sources for now.

Entry 3: Police and witnesses at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. The driver of the insured vehicle lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy.

Entry 4: The claimant reports a shoulder injury, and the kind and force of the crash appear to fit that injury well. No earlier injury to the same body area is known, and the claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Treatment has followed a usual course and has tapered off as the claimant improved. Nothing in the medical notes so far suggests the course of care has been unusual.

Entry 6: No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. Counsel has been informed that the claim is under ongoing review, and the file remains open pending the final medical summary.
